ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Gathering of the Whakapapa / Tā Moko

fullPassage:
Gathering of the Whakapapa

The phone rang, and it was my dad calling from my hometown, Waituhi.
"Can you take a week off?" he asked. "Your Nani Tama wants you here."
"But Dad!" I answered. "My boss won't let me take any more time off."
The phone went silent, and then I heard my grandfather say faintly, "I need your help, Grandson. I must go to Murupara to finish the whakapapa. Drive me there. Hurry, I may not have much time."
I just knew I had no choice. "All right, Nani," I replied with a sigh. "I'll come."

For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village genealogy, known as the whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, which ran through the house and destroyed our past. In only one night, everything we knew was gone. Nani Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter, my Auntie Hiraina.
Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands. He chanted the names of the ancestors, joining the past to the present once more. The village went quiet and listened to his chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our genealogy, searching back across the centuries. Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the middle of the chant. The village waited in worried silence until the next name burst out of his mouth. It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most of the whakapapa, but there were still missing names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to drive him to Murupara to finish his work.

When I arrived at Auntie's place, I was shocked to see how thin Nani Tama was.
"Look, Nani," I said. "I'm not taking you anywhere. You could die on me!"
Nani looked at me in anger.
"You want me to die here in this room? Looking at these four walls? When the whakapapa is not yet finished?"
The old man held on tightly to the side of the bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow, painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could not help but carry him to the car, and we set off with Auntie.

We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but wonderful to hear him. Sometimes, he burst into a song that he had taught Auntie. They sang together, lifting up their voices to send the song flying like a bird through the sky.

Just before noon, we arrived at a small town called Murupara.
"Where do we go now?" I asked Nani.
He did not reply, but he was searching inside himself, staring at the small houses. Then, at a street corner, he told us to turn. After turning the corner, we saw an old man standing in front of a house. He welcomed Nani Tama with a gentle smile, but in his eyes, I saw the message, "We must hurry."

Now that day seems like a dream to me. I remember the two old men sitting at the table and the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked. All through the quiet afternoon and into the evening, they recalled missing names. I had a strange feeling that there were other people in the room. I felt as if people from the past were looking over the shoulders of the two old men to see if the work was correct.
Finally, they stopped. It was done. After a moment of silence, the old man whispered to Nani, "Goodbye, friend." Crying, they pressed their noses together to say goodbye.

It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie's place. All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. Our hearts were full because our grandfather had saved our past for us.
Our Nani Tama smiled again. His smile grew tired.
He sighed. "At last, I may go now."
Then, he closed his eyes.
"No, Dad!" Auntie Hiraina cried.
The sun burst across the hills.

Deep Learning: Tā Moko: A Record of an Individual's Path

Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally significant practice of the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only decorative but also symbolic of an individual's journey from their past to their present. Each curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a person's whakapapa (genealogy), social positions, and personal accomplishments. This explains why no two tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head to be the most sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire faces, while women have it on their lips and chins. The Maori start getting these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are added to their tattoos to reflect their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a rite of passage throughout their lives. Although tā moko is less common these days, it is still practiced today by Maori people, who hope to preserve their traditions and heritage for the next generation.

questions.passage: The phone went silent, and then I heard my grandfather say (A)[faintly / loudly], "I need your help, Grandson. I must go to Murupara to finish the whakapapa." I just knew I had no choice. "All right, Nani," I replied with a (B)[sigh / laugh]. "I'll come." For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village (C)[genealogy / geography], known as the whakapapa.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 할아버지가 희미하게 말씀하셨다. 나는 한숨을 쉬며 대답했다. 마을의 족보를 기록하고 계셨다.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) faintly: 원문 그대로 '희미하게'. loudly(크게)는 병약한 할아버지 상황과 반대. ✅ (B) sigh: 원문 그대로 '한숨'. 마지못해 동의하는 상황이므로 laugh(웃음)는 부적절. ✅ (C) genealogy: 원문 그대로 '족보'. geography(지리)는 문맥 불일치.
det.tip: faintly: 희미하게, 어렴풋이. sigh: 한숨. genealogy: 족보, 계보 (= whakapapa).

questions.passage: Nani Tama, in (A)[despair / delight], went to stay with his daughter, my Auntie Hiraina. Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his (B)[shaky / steady] hands. He chanted the names of the (C)[ancestors / descendants], joining the past to the present once more.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 나니 타마는 절망 속에 딸의 집으로 갔다. 떨리는 손으로 족보를 다시 쓰기 시작했다. 조상들의 이름을 외웠다.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) despair: 원문 그대로 '절망'. 화재로 모든 것을 잃었으므로 delight(기쁨)는 반대. ✅ (B) shaky: 원문 그대로 '떨리는'. 노쇠한 할아버지이므로 steady(안정된)는 부적절. ✅ (C) ancestors: 원문 그대로 '조상'. 족보는 과거를 기록하므로 descendants(후손)는 반대.
det.tip: despair: 절망 ↔ delight: 기쁨. shaky: 떨리는 ↔ steady: 안정된. ancestors: 조상 ↔ descendants: 후손.

questions.passage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally (A)[significant / insignificant] practice of the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only (B)[decorative / destructive] but also symbolic of an individual's journey. Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a rite of (C)[passage / punishment] throughout their lives.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 문화적으로 중요한 관행이었다. 장식적일 뿐만 아니라 상징적이기도 하다. 삶의 통과 의례로서 큰 중요성을 지녔다.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) significant: 원문 그대로 '중요한'. insignificant(중요하지 않은)는 수천 년간 지속된 문화와 반대. ✅ (B) decorative: 원문 그대로 '장식적인'. destructive(파괴적인)는 예술과 반대. ✅ (C) passage: 원문 'rite of passage(통과 의례)'. punishment(처벌)는 문맥 불일치.
det.tip: significant(중요한) ↔ insignificant. decorative(장식적인) ↔ destructive(파괴적인). rite of passage: 통과 의례.

questions.passage: But then came the night of the fire, which ran through the house and ①<u>destroyed</u> our past. In only one night, everything we knew was gone. Nani Tama, in ②<u>despair</u>, went to stay with his daughter, my Auntie Hiraina. Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his ③<u>shaky</u> hands. He chanted the names of the ancestors, joining the past to the ④<u>future</u> once more.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 조상의 이름을 외우며 과거를 현재(present)에 다시 연결했다. future(미래)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①destroyed(파괴했다): 화재가 집을 파괴한 원문 그대로. ✅ ②despair(절망): 모든 것을 잃은 상황에 적절. ✅ ③shaky(떨리는): 노쇠한 할아버지의 손 묘사로 적절. ❌ ④future(미래): 원문은 present(현재). 족보는 '과거를 현재에 연결'하는 것이므로 future는 부적절.
det.tip: joining the past to the present = 과거를 현재에 연결하다. present(현재) ↔ future(미래).

questions.passage: The old man held on tightly to the side of the bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow, ①<u>painful</u> step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could not help but carry him to the car, and we set off with Auntie. We traveled all night, mostly in ②<u>silence</u>, listening to Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but ③<u>wonderful</u> to hear him. Sometimes, he burst into a song that he had taught Auntie. They sang together, lifting up their voices to send the song ④<u>sinking</u> like a bird through the sky.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 목소리를 높여 노래를 새처럼 하늘을 날리듯(flying) 보냈다. sinking(가라앉는)은 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①painful(고통스러운): 한 걸음마다 아팠다는 원문 그대로. ✅ ②silence(침묵): 대부분 침묵 속에 여행했다는 원문 그대로. ✅ ③wonderful(멋진): 기묘하지만 멋진 경험이라는 원문 그대로. ❌ ④sinking(가라앉는): 원문은 flying(날아가는). 새처럼 하늘을 날아간다는 비유이므로 sinking은 반대.
det.tip: flying(날아가는) ↔ sinking(가라앉는). send ~ flying like a bird = ~를 새처럼 날려 보내다.

questions.passage: He did not reply, but he was searching inside himself, staring at the small houses. Then, at a street corner, he told us to turn. After turning the corner, we saw an old man standing in front of a house. He ①<u>welcomed</u> Nani Tama with a gentle smile, but in his eyes, I saw the message, "We must hurry." All through the quiet afternoon and into the evening, they ②<u>recalled</u> missing names. I had a strange feeling that there were other people in the room. I felt as if people from the past were looking over the ③<u>shoulders</u> of the two old men to see if the work was ④<u>flawed</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 과거의 사람들이 두 노인의 어깨 너머로 작업이 올바른지(correct) 확인하는 것 같았다. flawed(결함 있는)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①welcomed(환영했다): 부드러운 미소로 환영했다는 원문 그대로. ✅ ②recalled(회상했다): 빠진 이름을 회상했다는 원문 그대로. ✅ ③shoulders(어깨): 어깨 너머로 봤다는 원문 그대로. ❌ ④flawed(결함 있는): 원문은 correct(올바른). 조상들이 작업이 정확한지 확인한다는 맥락이므로 flawed는 반대.
det.tip: correct(올바른) ↔ flawed(결함 있는). look over one's shoulder = ~의 어깨 너머로 보다.

questions.passage: The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, which ran through the house and destroyed our past. In only one night, everything we knew was gone. Nani Tama, in __________, went to stay with his daughter, my Auntie Hiraina. Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나니 타마는 절망 속에 딸의 집으로 갔다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③despair(절망): 화재로 족보를 포함한 모든 것을 잃었으므로 절망이 적절. ❌ ①anger(분노): 분노보다는 상실감이 핵심. ❌ ②relief(안도): 재앙 후 안도는 부적절. ❌ ④confusion(혼란): 상황은 명확하므로 혼란보다 절망.
det.tip: in despair = 절망에 빠져. despair: 절망 ↔ hope: 희망. ashes of the past = 과거의 잔해.

questions.passage: His voice traveled along the lines of our genealogy, searching back across the centuries. Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the middle of the chant. The village waited in worried __________ until the next name burst out of his mouth. It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most of the whakapapa.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 마을은 걱정스러운 침묵 속에 기다렸다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②silence(침묵): 이름이 기억나지 않아 목소리가 멈추자 마을이 걱정스러운 침묵 속에 기다렸다. ❌ ①celebration(축하): 걱정스러운 상황과 반대. ❌ ③chanting(구송): 이미 멈춘 상황. ❌ ④applause(박수): 걱정스러운 분위기와 불일치.
det.tip: in worried silence = 걱정스러운 침묵 속에. burst out of = ~에서 터져 나오다.

questions.passage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally significant practice of the Maori for thousands of years. Each curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a person's whakapapa, social positions, and personal accomplishments. This explains why no two tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head to be the most __________ part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire faces, while women have it on their lips and chins.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 마오리족은 전통적으로 머리를 신체에서 가장 신성한 부분으로 여겨왔다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④sacred(신성한): 머리를 가장 신성한 부분으로 여겨 얼굴에 문신한다는 원문 맥락. ❌ ①visible(보이는): 보이기 때문이 아니라 신성하기 때문. ❌ ②ordinary(평범한): 가장 평범하다면 굳이 문신할 이유 없음. ❌ ③vulnerable(취약한): 취약함과 문신 문화는 무관.
det.tip: sacred: 신성한, 성스러운. rite of passage: 통과 의례. accomplishment: 업적, 성취.

questions.passage: But then came the night of the fire, which ran through the house and <u>destroyed</u> our past. In only one night, everything we knew was gone.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 destroyed와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 화재가 집을 관통하며 우리의 과거를 파괴했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①ruined(파괴했다): destroyed와 동의어. ❌ ②preserved(보존했다): 반의어. ❌ ③revealed(드러냈다): 파괴와 무관. ❌ ④scattered(흩뿌렸다): 유사하지만 파괴의 의미는 아님.
det.tip: destroy = ruin = demolish (파괴하다). destroy ↔ preserve(보존하다).

questions.passage: He chanted the names of the ancestors, joining the past to the present once more. His voice traveled along the lines of our genealogy, searching back across the <u>centuries</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 centuries와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 그의 목소리는 수세기를 거슬러 올라가며 찾았다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ages(시대, 오랜 세월): centuries(세기)와 유사하게 긴 시간을 의미. ❌ ①decades(수십 년): 세기보다 짧은 단위. ❌ ②moments(순간): 반대 의미. ❌ ④seasons(계절): 시간 길이가 전혀 다름.
det.tip: century: 100년, 세기. ages: 오랜 세월. decades: 10년 단위. across the centuries = 수세기에 걸쳐.

questions.passage: I had a strange feeling that there were other people in the room. I felt as if people from the past were looking over the shoulders of the two old men to see if the work was correct. Finally, they stopped. It was done. After a moment of silence, the old man <u>whispered</u> to Nani, "Goodbye, friend."
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 whispered와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 노인이 나니에게 "잘 가게, 친구."라고 속삭였다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②murmured(중얼거렸다): whispered와 유사하게 조용히 말하는 것. ❌ ①shouted(소리쳤다): 반의어. ❌ ③announced(발표했다): 공식적 선언으로 속삭임과 반대. ❌ ④demanded(요구했다): 강한 어조로 속삭임과 반대.
det.tip: whisper = murmur (속삭이다, 중얼거리다). whisper ↔ shout(소리치다).

questions.passage: It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie's place. All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling, Nani Tama <u>lifted up</u> the whakapapa and offered it to the village.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 lifted up과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 나니 타마가 족보를 들어 올려 마을에 바쳤다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③lowered(낮추었다): lifted up(들어 올리다)의 반의어. ❌ ①raised(올렸다): 동의어. ❌ ②held(잡았다): 유사 동작이지 반대가 아님. ❌ ④displayed(전시했다): 관련 있지만 반의어 아님.
det.tip: lift up = raise (들어 올리다) ↔ lower(낮추다). offer: 바치다, 제공하다.

questions.passage: Although tā moko is less common these days, it is still practiced today by Maori people, who hope to <u>preserve</u> their traditions and heritage for the next generation.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 preserve와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 마오리족은 다음 세대를 위해 전통과 유산을 보존하기를 희망한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①abandon(포기하다): preserve(보존하다)의 반의어. ❌ ②maintain(유지하다): 동의어. ❌ ③protect(보호하다): 유사 의미. ❌ ④cherish(소중히 여기다): 유사 의미.
det.tip: preserve = maintain = protect (보존하다) ↔ abandon = give up (포기하다). heritage: 유산.

questions.passage:
(A) The phone went silent, and then I heard my grandfather say faintly, "I need your help, Grandson." I just knew I had no <u>choice</u>.

(B) When an octopus encounters its hunter or prey, it must decide very quickly which color, pattern, and texture to <u>choose</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)의 choice와 (B)의 choose가 각각 의미하는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) '선택의 여지가 없었다'에서 choice = 대안, 다른 방법. (B) '어떤 것을 고를지'에서 choose = 고르다, 선택하다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: (A) 'had no choice'는 '대안이 없다'는 의미로 choice=대안. (B) 'which ~ to choose'는 '어떤 것을 고르다'로 choose=고르다. ❌ ①: (A)는 '선택권'보다 '대안'이 더 정확. ❌ ③④: 품사와 의미가 뒤바뀜.
det.tip: have no choice = 대안이 없다(= have no alternative). choose: (여러 중) 고르다. choice(명사) ↔ choose(동사).

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a record of the members of a family over a long period, showing how they are related to each other"

det.korean: 가족 구성원의 오랜 기간에 걸친 기록으로, 서로의 관계를 보여주는 것 = 족보(genealogy).
det.analysis: ✅ ③genealogy(족보): 가족 관계 기록을 뜻하는 정확한 단어. ❌ ①heritage(유산): 문화/전통 유산으로 가족 기록과 다름. ❌ ②tradition(전통): 관습이지 가족 기록이 아님. ❌ ④mythology(신화): 신화와 족보는 다름.
det.tip: genealogy: 족보, 계보 (gene=유전자 + logy=학문). whakapapa = 마오리어로 genealogy.

questions.passage: Nani Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter. Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands. He __________ (chant) the names of the ancestors, joining the past to the present once more.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 나니는 조상들의 이름을 외웠다(chanted).
det.analysis: ✅ chanted: 과거 시제. 앞 문장 'went', 'began' 등 과거형과 병렬. 현재형이나 진행형은 시제 불일치.
det.tip: chant: 구송하다, 외우다. 과거 시제 통일: went → began → chanted.

questions.passage: The Maori start getting these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are __________ (add) to their tattoos to reflect their life experiences.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 나이가 들수록 더 많은 선과 모양이 문신에 추가된다(added).
det.analysis: ✅ added: 수동태 'are added'. 주어 'more lines and shapes'가 추가되는 대상이므로 수동. 'are + p.p.' 구조.
det.tip: are added: 수동태(be + p.p.). add-added-added. reflect: 반영하다.

questions.passage: When I arrived at Auntie's place, I was shocked to see how thin Nani Tama was. "Look, Nani," I said. "I'm not taking you anywhere. You could die on me!" Nani looked at me in anger. The old man held on tightly to the side of the bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow, painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could not help but __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 할아버지를 차까지 데려다 드릴 수밖에 없었다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①carry him to the car: 원문 표현. 걸으려 안간힘 쓰는 할아버지를 차까지 안아 드렸다. ❌ ②leave him behind: 두고 가는 것은 전체 맥락과 반대. ❌ ③call the doctor: 의사를 부른다는 내용 없음. ❌ ④refuse his request: 이미 거절했다가 마음을 바꾼 상황.
det.tip: could not help but V = ~하지 않을 수 없었다. set off = 출발하다.

questions.passage: It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie's place. All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. Our hearts were full because our grandfather had __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 할아버지가 우리의 과거를 구해주셨기 때문에 마음이 벅찼다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③saved our past for us: 원문 그대로. 족보를 완성해 마을의 역사를 보존했다. ❌ ①returned home safely: 안전 귀환이 아니라 족보 완성이 핵심. ❌ ②completed the journey alone: 혼자 완성한 게 아니라 무루파라의 노인과 함께. ❌ ④forgiven the village people: 용서와 관련 없는 맥락.
det.tip: Our hearts were full = 마음이 벅찼다. save our past = 우리의 과거를 구하다/보존하다.
